title: When Validators and Repairs See the Same Candidate: A Confirmatory Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, confirmatory experiment that evaluated a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The experiment used gpt-5-mini to synthesize device-level configuration change sequences for 250 synthetic intent-to-configuration tasks (one shared initial generation per task; no retrieval augmentation), and a deterministic network validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) to classify actionable misconfigurations. Under the executed conditions (shared initial candidate; a single sampled generation per task; temperature unset), every initial candidate passed the validator (n=250/250), and the guarded pipeline applied no repairs: baseline and guarded validity rates were both 1.0 (n11=250, n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered primary paired estimand (guarded minus baseline actionable-misconfiguration rate) was 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p=1.0; 95% CI [0.0,0.0] via paired bootstrap). A key preregistered objective concerned induction of misconfigurations by poisoned retrieval context; however, the executed adapter configuration did not perform retrieval-augmented generation, so that poison-related hypotheses were not testable in this run. We therefore interpret results narrowly: when a single-shot initial candidate (the same candidate seen by baseline and guarded arms) is already valid under a deterministic validator, the guarded pipeline produced no change. We document the preregistration, frozen execution manifest, and all artifacts; discuss construct and external-validity limits (synthetic tasks, single model, single validator, no RAG), and outline priority follow-ups that (a) enable controlled injected retrieval contexts, (b) expand validator realism, and (c) evaluate multi-model and RAG-enabled pipelines under adversarial retrieval.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as components of intent-based NetOps: translating operator intent into low-level device configuration, planning staged changes, and generating remediation sequences [1,2]. Because LLM outputs can omit implicit ordering constraints or violate operational invariants, architectures that pair generation with deterministic validators and limited repair (generate→validate→repair, hereafter guarded) are widely advocated as practical safety controls [3,4]. Prior work has proposed such guarded designs and provided controlled demonstrations and benchmarks, but open questions remain about their empirical effect-size under operationally meaningful controls (paired comparisons, identical initial candidate sampling semantics, and explicit preregistration) and under adversarial retrieval or poisoned context attacks [2,5].

This study was preregistered. The intended high-level research question was: to what extent can targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts induce actionable misconfigurations in an LLM-driven NetOps pipeline that uses retrieved artifacts as grounding? The executed experiment, however, ran under shared_initial_candidate semantics with retrieval-augmented generation disabled; consequently the executed estimand measured the guarded pipeline's paired effect on a single shared initial candidate versus the baseline single-shot validity of that candidate. We report the executed design, results, interpretation, and limitations clearly and exhaustively.
sections.related_work: LLMs for NetOps and intent-based translation have been surveyed and prototyped in recent literature, including task-driven configuration generation and RAG/tool-augmented workflows [1,2,6]. Concerns about LLM hallucination and constraint violations in operational domains are well documented and motivate validators and tool augmentation [7,8]. Tool-augmented agents and multi-agent orchestration proposals argue that external verifiers (e.g., Batfish or deterministic configuration validators) can reduce factual errors, but also introduce latency and system-complexity tradeoffs [3,4,9]. Adversarial work in adjacent domains (RAG pipelines for security operations) demonstrates that poisoned retrieval contexts can induce targeted hallucinations and actionable errors, motivating NetOps-specific adversarial benchmarks [5]. Our study situates itself as a small-scale, tightly preregistered empirical probe into a guarded pipeline's paired effect when the baseline and guarded arms share the same initial sampled candidate.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: We preregistered the study (candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1) and specified a paired design. The preregistered primary estimand named an effect of poisoned retrieval on actionable misconfiguration rate. The frozen execution contract that was actually run used generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate, retrieval_augmented_generation=false, and exactly one sampled initial generation per task; therefore the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration (guarded minus baseline) when baseline and guarded begin from the same single sampled initial candidate and the validator/repair logic is permitted only in the guarded arm.

Tasks and validator: We used 250 synthetic intent-to-configuration tasks generated deterministically from a registered task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task describes an intent and a constrained change workflow (examples and full task payloads are archived). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implements rule-based checks for reachability, ordering constraints, and forbidden touches; it emits a binary actionable_misconfig indicator and structured violation codes.

Model and sampling: The host model declared was gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. The recorded model configuration set temperature=null/unset; per preregistration and the methods requirements we state explicitly that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be equated with temperature=0. Exactly one initial generation per task was sampled and reused under shared_initial_candidate semantics across baseline and guarded conditions; no independent baseline-versus-guarded sampling occurred. Adapter constraints limited repair attempts to at most one validator-triggered repair per task.

Design details and outcome: For each of 250 tasks we obtained a single shared initial generation from the model; the baseline outcome recorded initial candidate validity under the validator. The guarded pipeline applied deterministic validation and permitted one repair attempt when the validator reported violations; final guarded outcome recorded the validator result after any permitted repair. The primary outcome is the per-task paired binary indicator actionable_misconfig (1 if the final output would cause an actionable misconfiguration; 0 otherwise). Statistical plan: a confirmatory paired test (exact McNemar two-sided) at alpha=0.05; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples) reported 95% CI. All analysis code, seeds and raw outputs were archived.
sections.results:
Execution and artifact summary: The preregistered run completed as recorded in the frozen execution manifest (started 2026-08-31; completed 2026-08-31). Planned episodes 500 (two conditions × 250 tasks) were completed with zero failed episodes; provider call audit shows 250 model-call events corresponding to the shared initial generation stage. All raw model outputs, validator traces, and repair traces are archived in the execution bundle.

Primary confirmatory outcome: Across 250 complete paired task episodes the contingency counts were n11=250, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Baseline actionable-misconfig rate = 250/250 = 1.0 (note: success indicating VALID_CONFIGURATION per scorer semantics), guarded actionable-misconfig rate = 250/250 = 1.0. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p=1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap resamples=10,000; seed=1729). The validator traces show that no repair action was applied in any guarded episode (repair_applied=false for all guarded traces). Representative per-task artifacts (task-000004..task-000008) and their shared initial candidates are in the archived execution bundle; they match exactly across baseline and guarded arms under shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Deviation relative to poisoning objectives: The preregistration included hypotheses about poisoned retrieval contexts and a dose–response exploratory plan. The executed adapter configuration did not perform retrieval-augmented generation (retrieval_augmented_generation=false), and no poisoned retrieval fragments were injected. Consequently the preregistered poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run; this deviation is disclosed and discussed in the Limitations and Threats sections.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation: Under the exact execution semantics (shared initial candidate, single sampled generation reused across arms, deterministic validator, no RAG), every sampled initial candidate satisfied the validator, thus producing maximal baseline validity. Since shared_initial_candidate semantics guarantee the same initial candidate for baseline and guarded arms, the guarded pipeline could only change outcomes via repair; because the validator accepted all initial candidates no repair was invoked and no paired effect was observed. This is a narrow but valid empirical conclusion: for these synthetic tasks, model sampling seed choices, and validator model, the guarded pipeline did not alter final validity.

Implications: The result does not imply that guarded pipelines are unnecessary in general. Rather, it highlights that a guarded pipeline's marginal benefit depends critically on (a) the base rate of invalid initial candidates under the chosen model and prompt, (b) whether the pipeline uses independent generation or shared_initial_candidate semantics, and (c) whether external retrieval or adversarially poisoned context can alter initial candidate content. The absence of RAG in this execution prevented evaluation of retrieval-poisoning risks, which remain open and arguably central to operational threat models.

Threats to validity: Internal validity — shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced per the adapter; this design isolates validator/repair effects but prevents measurement of generation variability across arms. The recorded model temperature was unset; we explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling. Construct validity — the validator is deterministic and rule-based but may not capture all production failure modes (e.g., vendor-specific semantics, dynamic route convergence). External validity — synthetic task families, one model (gpt-5-mini), and a single validator limit generalization to diverse production topologies and multi-vendor environments. Conclusion validity — paired sample size (N=250) provided adequate power for the preregistered effect sizes, but here the observed effect was exactly zero because of complete baseline success. The most important operational threat that this run cannot address is the effectiveness of guarded pipelines against poisoned retrievals or adversarial context; that question must be addressed in a follow-up execution enabling controlled RAG and poisoning injection.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered paired experiment examining a guarded LLM→NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The executed run (gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator; retrieval disabled) found no paired difference because every shared initial candidate passed the validator and no repairs were applied. The study demonstrates the importance of aligning execution semantics with the targeted estimand: shared_initial_candidate designs isolate validator/repair effects but cannot by themselves reveal generation variability or retrieval-based attack vulnerabilities. Future work should (1) enable controlled retrieval augmentation and adversarially injected contexts to evaluate poisoning hypotheses directly, (2) test multi-model and multi-validator ensembles, and (3) measure latency, operator triage cost, and production-representative validator realism. All execution artifacts and analysis scripts are archived to support reproducibility and follow-up experiments.

limitations: Executed run used shared_initial_candidate semantics and a single sampled initial generation per task; therefore results measure validator/repair effects on the same candidate, not independent generation variability.
Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter; the preregistered poisoning hypotheses (RAG-poison dose–response) were not testable in this run.
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used; external validity to other models, validators, vendors, and production topologies is limited.
Tasks were synthetic intent→configuration instances designed to exercise ordering/dependency constraints; they do not substitute for large-scale production deployment evaluations.
Temperature was recorded as null/unset in the model configuration; null does not imply deterministic sampling—model-side nondeterminism remains possible and is logged in the execution artifacts.
